Figure 1. Conceptual illustration of Echo. The agent learns from experience and discovers transferable patterns, enabling interpretable
analogy-based reasoning and cross-task generalization. In some classical methods, such as DEPS [44] and JARVIS-1 [45], ICL is mainly
used to retrieve few-shots from the memory bank to assist in generating sub-task sequences for the current goal. Echo, on the other hand,
treats ICL learning as an active process — it proactively retrieves potentially new tasks from the memory bank for validation and execution.

                                                                                                          different tasks and infer what prior experience remains ap-
                                 Abstract                                                                 plicable in new situations. Building on this formulation,
                                                                                                          Echo leverages In-Context Analogy Learning (ICAL) to re-
    Multimodal LLM agents operating in complex game en-                                                   trieve relevant experiences and adapt them to unseen tasks
vironments must continually reuse past experience to solve                                                through contextual examples. Experiments in Minecraft
new tasks efficiently. In this work, we propose Echo, a                                                   show that, under a from-scratch learning setting, Echo
transfer-oriented memory framework that enables agents                                                    achieves a 1.3×–1.7× speed-up on object-unlocking tasks.
to derive actionable knowledge from prior interactions                                                    Moreover, Echo exhibits a burst-like chain-unlocking phe-
rather than treating memory as a passive repository of                                                    nomenon, rapidly unlocking multiple similar items within a
static records. To make transfer explicit, Echo decomposes                                                short time interval after acquiring transferable experience.
reusable knowledge into five dimensions: structure, at-                                                   These results suggest that experience transfer is a promis-
tribute, process, function, and interaction. This formulation                                             ing direction for improving the efficiency and adaptability
allows the agent to identify recurring patterns shared across                                             of multimodal LLM agents in complex interactive environ-
                                                                                                          ments.

1. Introduction
Driven by embodied intelligence and complex interactive                      Tech Line
                                                                                         Rapid Unlocking
tasks, planning-oriented multimodal large language model
(MLLM) agents have rapidly emerged [36, 38, 42, 44, 45,
51, 57]. Representative works such as Voyager [42] and
JARVIS-1 [45] in environments like Minecraft demonstrate
open-ended exploration driven by a “perception-reasoning-                                                  1.3×Faster

action-memory” loop, where agents continuously self-                                                             1.7×Faster

improve through environmental feedback. These systems
reveal the potential to decompose goals, plan subtasks, and
invoke tools without large-scale task-specific supervision.

and evaluate cross-modal correspondences along five inter-

and interaction.                                                • Procedural Axis—“How the world changes.” Captures
    These five dimensions are not arbitrary-they form a           the causal rules and state transitions that define how ac-
holistic grammar of understanding for any agent operating         tions alter the environment. It models sequences and
in open-world environments. From a theoretical standpoint,        dependencies—clarifying what to do, when, and why.
an embodied agent seeking to transfer or reconstruct knowl-     • Functional Axis—“What things do.” Describes the pur-
edge must simultaneously grasp three fundamental ques-            pose and role of objects—what they can do and how they
tions:                                                            contribute to tasks. It supports semantic-level generaliza-
• What the world is like—captured through its structures          tion and creative reuse across domains.
   and attributes;                                              • Interaction Axis—“How the agent interacts with the
• How the world changes—revealed through its proce-               world.” Characterizes the perception–action loop, show-
   dures and functions;                                           ing how operations lead to feedback and environmental
• How the agent engages with the world—embodied in                response. It connects knowledge to execution, ensuring
   its interactions.                                              actions are both understandable and performable.

sion closes the loop, modeling the continuous feedback be-      multimodal inputs—visual, textual, and interactive—into a
tween perception and action that allows an agent to learn       unified, comparable, and verifiable semantic snapshot. This
not only from observation but from participation. Although      unified representation enables Echo to perform stable re-

• The Procedural axis has the greatest impact on long-
   horizon tasks (e.g., Crafting Chain). Removing it leads
   to severe degradation (-12%).
• The Functional axis dominates functional equivalence
   tasks. Removing it almost disables the tasks (-9%).
• The Interaction axis affects short-term tasks. Removing                      (a) Find planks             (b) Craft wooden pickaxe
   it causes a major drop in Utility Blocks (-7%).
The experimental results show that removing a single axis
causes a significant performance drop, much greater than
the drop when only retaining a single axis. The Structural
axis primarily affects geometric and recipe-related tasks;
the Attribute axis is crucial for functional equivalence and
                                                                               (c) Find stones              (d) Craft stone pickaxe
crafting chain tasks; the Procedural axis has a decisive im-
pact on long-horizon tasks like Crafting Chain and Crafting            Figure 9. Transferring from a wooden pickaxe to a stone pickaxe.
Table; the Functional axis dominates functional equivalence
tasks; and the Interaction axis strongly influences utilities
operation tasks. Explicit transfer axes help clarify the de-
pendencies between tasks and effectively locate the sources
of errors, such as process reasoning errors or interface posi-      5. Conclusion and Discussion
